newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's SFE plans finer, broader wool futures.
newsitem.headline: Australia's SFE plans finer, broader wool futures.

text.p: The Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) will list two new wool futures contracts, chief executive Les Hosking said on Thursday.
The new contracts will be for a finer wool contract, likely to 19.5 micron, and a broader wool contract, likely to be 23 micron wool, to be traded alongside the existing 21 micron contract, he said.

In a statement released to coincide with the Wool Council of Australia's (WCA) annual conference, Hosking said the launch of the two new contracts would provide wool market participants with wider scope to tailor their hedging and risk management.
WCA president Rod Thirkell-Johnston said the decision marked another step forward in laying down machinery to develop forward markets.
The new contracts will complement the existing contract and reflect the fact that fine, medium and broader wool prices frequently diverge, creating a basis risk in hedging these wools, he said.
Since the launch of the 21 micron contract two years ago activity in the contract has continued to increase.
Last week the open position in the contract topped 1,000 contracts for the first time reflecting the growing interest in wool futures by industry participants, Hosking said.
The wool industry had undertaken significant change in recent years including a renewed emphasis on utilising price risk management tools such as wool futures and options, he said.
The new wool futures contracts will be cash settled.
The 21 micron contract will remain a physically deliverable contract.
